questions.q: Which occupancy needs panic hardware on its required exits?
questions.n: Assembly occupancies with crowds need it.

questions.q: Frameless shower glass is usually:
questions.n: Frameless panels need about 10 mm tempered glass to be self-supporting.

questions.q: By day you can't see in, but at night with the lights on everyone can. Which glass behaves like this?
questions.n: Reflective coatings mirror whichever side is brighter.

questions.q: Panic hardware exists mainly to:
o: Release the latch easily under pressure
questions.n: Pushing the bar unlatches the door.

questions.q: A low-cost railing steel with poor corrosion resistance that must be painted or coated is:
questions.n: Plain carbon steel rusts unless protected.

questions.q: Laminated glass gets its sound reduction from which interlayer?
questions.n: PVB damps vibration; acoustic grades go further.

questions.q: A kitchen opens onto an outdoor dining terrace for serving and casual interaction. Which opening suits it?
o: A full-height sliding glass door with an insect screen
questions.n: A wide operable slider gives open passage between kitchen and terrace.

questions.q: Typical stock door jamb thickness:
questions.n: 2" × 4" or 2" × 5" jambs are common.

questions.q: For handrails in a clinic, the most hygienic material is:
questions.n: Stainless steel is non-porous and easy to disinfect.

questions.q: Exterior railings near the sea should use which stainless grade?
questions.n: 316 contains molybdenum, which resists chloride pitting.

questions.q: The most common stainless steel grade, used everywhere for its cost and corrosion resistance, is:
questions.n: Type 304 is the workhorse grade.

questions.q: Which glass is tempered so that it shatters into small, blunt granules?
questions.n: Full tempering makes the glass about four times stronger and breaks it safely.

questions.q: Bathroom windows and doors that need light but privacy usually get:
questions.n: The textured surface obscures the view.

questions.q: Shopfronts and big industrial openings are usually closed with:
questions.n: Roll-up shutters coil overhead and secure wide openings.

questions.q: Safety glazing is NOT required for:
o: Glass within 24" of a door edge
A sidelite whose sill is more than 18" (457 mm) above the floor and meets the other exemptions
A sidelite with a sill under 18"
questions.n: Raised sills reduce the human-impact risk.

questions.q: For indoor railings, the usual stainless steel grade is:
questions.n: 304 is enough indoors; 316 is kept for marine or exterior exposure.

questions.q: In glazing terms, the putty bevel on the outside of the pane is the:
questions.n: Face putty is the exterior triangular bead; bedding sits behind the glass.

questions.q: On a lockset, the distance from the door edge to the center of the knob hole is the:
questions.n: Common backsets are 60 mm and 70 mm.

questions.q: Heavy steel gates commonly hang on:
questions.n: Weld-on barrel hinges carry heavy steel leaves.

questions.q: The cast fitting that holds frameless facade glass at its drilled corners is a:
questions.n: Spiders transfer point loads from bolted glass to the structure.

questions.q: The percentage of visible light a glazing transmits is its:
questions.n: Visible light transmittance.

questions.q: Which hinge actively slows the door so it can't slam?
questions.n: Soft-close hinges damp the last part of the swing.

questions.q: Ceramic patterns fused onto the glass surface for glare and solar control describe:
questions.n: Frit is ceramic enamel fired onto the glass.

questions.q: The barrier along a balcony or stair edge that keeps people from falling is the:
questions.n: Guardrails protect open edges; handrails are for grip.

questions.q: A garden-facing window alcove projects from the wall: a big fixed center pane flanked by two smaller operable sides, deep enough for a reading seat. This is a:
questions.n: A bay window projects outward with a central fixed pane and angled operable sides.

questions.q: Which glass type is mainly an envelope product and seldom needed for interior partitions?
questions.n: Low-E controls heat flow through the envelope; indoors there's little to control.

questions.q: In a car, the windshield is laminated. The side and rear windows are usually:
questions.n: Side and rear glass is tempered so it crumbles into blunt pieces.

questions.q: Which door type should NOT be used as an exit door?
questions.n: Exits must be side-swinging, not overhead or rolling.

questions.q: Which of these is door hardware?
questions.n: Hardware means the metal fittings; jambs and leaves are the door itself.

questions.q: For extra security on a main entrance, add a:
questions.n: A deadbolt throws a solid bolt that can't be pushed back without the key.

questions.q: A frameless glass balustrade fixed to the slab edge at discrete points uses:
questions.n: Standoffs give a floating, point-fixed look.

questions.q: In a framed shower enclosure, the frame supports the glass, so the minimum tempered thickness commonly used is:
questions.n: Framed enclosures can go down to about 6 mm tempered.

questions.q: A balcony door that folds into a stack at one side instead of swinging out is a:
questions.n: Bifold leaves fold together, saving swing space.

questions.q: A display case where security, strength and safety come first:
questions.n: Laminated glass resists smash-through and holds together.

questions.q: Stock height of a shower glass partition is about:
questions.n: 1.8 m is the common ready-made height.

questions.q: Vision panels in fire exit doors must be:
questions.n: The glass must match the door's fire rating.

questions.q: For an office building, the sturdiest standard lockset is the:
questions.n: Mortise locks are heavy-duty and versatile.

questions.q: "Standard" glass with no strengthening treatment is:
questions.n: Annealed glass is cooled slowly and has no built-in stress.

questions.q: A communicating door between two rooms, opening either way, uses which jamb?
questions.n: Double rabbets give a stop for either swing.

questions.q: Coastal house, high-touch interior knobs: corrosion-resistant, naturally antimicrobial, heavy and solid, without the fast patina of pure copper. Which?
questions.n: Brass is copper-based (antimicrobial), corrosion-resistant and tarnishes slowly.

questions.q: Molten glass floated on molten tin gives flat, even sheets without polishing. Before any further treatment this is:
questions.n: The float process makes annealed glass that is later tempered or laminated as needed.
